questions.q: What happens when SELECT CAST('not a number' AS INT); runs?
options: SQL Server raises a conversion error and the batch stops
questions.explain: Plain CAST is all-or-nothing — a failing conversion raises an error (Msg 245) and halts the batch.

questions.q: What does TRY_CAST('not a number' AS INT) return?
questions.explain: TRY_CAST attempts the conversion and returns NULL instead of raising an error when it fails.

questions.q: What is the relationship between TRY_CONVERT and CONVERT?
options: TRY_CONVERT only works with date types, unlike CONVERT
TRY_CONVERT and CONVERT are unrelated functions
TRY_CONVERT requires fewer arguments than CONVERT
TRY_CONVERT has the same signature as CONVERT, including the optional style argument, but returns NULL instead of erroring on failure
questions.explain: TRY_CONVERT mirrors CONVERT's full signature, including the style number, but fails gracefully with NULL.

questions.q: In the PhoneNumber cleanup query, what does a returned row with DigitsOnly IS NULL mean?
options: That row has a NULL PhoneNumber value
That row was deleted by the query
That phone number, even after stripping dashes and parentheses, still didn't convert cleanly to a plain number
questions.explain: TRY_CAST returns NULL only when the conversion would have failed — meaning something other than digits remained after cleanup.

questions.q: Why would a developer prefer TRY_CAST over CAST when cleaning or validating incoming data?
options: TRY_CAST is faster than CAST in every case
TRY_CAST lets the query keep running and flag bad values with NULL, instead of crashing the entire batch on the first bad row
TRY_CAST can convert data types that CAST cannot
questions.explain: TRY_CAST's whole purpose is graceful failure — identifying problem rows with NULL rather than stopping the batch.
